name: Enterprise Cloud Platform – Cloud Service Roadmap
disclaimer: This roadmap reflects the current Azure Landing Zone governance decisions of the Enterprise Cloud Platform team. It is generated from the master Cloud Service Roadmap Excel workbook, which remains the formal source of truth. Denied and restricted services may be requestable through the Exception & Deviation process; approval is never guaranteed and always requires review by the Cloud Governance Board.

subscriptionTypes.name: vNET / Private
subscriptionTypes.description: Intranet applications with direct network connectivity to the corporate vNET and on-premises data centers via the hub-spoke topology.

subscriptionTypes.name: External / Public
subscriptionTypes.description: Internet-facing applications with no direct connectivity to the corporate vNET or on-prem; internal integration must go through the Cloud Integration Platform.

enterpriseServices.name: Enterprise AI Foundry Service
enterpriseServices.description: Centrally managed Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI offering. Provides governed access to foundation models, prompt flow, and model deployment without individual teams standing up their own AI Foundry or OpenAI resources. Includes cost chargeback, content-safety guardrails, and pre-approved model catalog.

enterpriseServices.name: Enterprise Data Platform
enterpriseServices.description: Central analytics and data-integration platform covering ingestion, curated lakehouse zones, and enterprise reporting. Replaces individually deployed Synapse workspaces and Data Factory instances with a governed, shared-cost, multi-tenant platform.

enterpriseServices.name: Cloud Integration Platform
enterpriseServices.description: The approved pattern for connectivity between internal (vNET/private) systems and external (public/internet-facing) applications. Since external subscriptions have no direct network path to the corporate vNET or on-premises data centers, all internal-to-external integration must route through this platform's managed APIs, message relays, and gateway patterns.

enterpriseServices.name: Lab-as-a-Service
enterpriseServices.description: Centrally managed sandbox and training-lab environments with automatic expiry, cost caps, and pre-approved images. Replaces ad hoc use of Azure DevTest Labs in individual subscriptions.

regions.name: West Europe
regions.notes: Primary EU hub region for both subscription types.

regions.name: North Europe
regions.notes: Secondary EU hub region; paired with West Europe for high availability.

regions.name: Germany West Central
regions.notes: Private only. Reserved for Germany data-residency workloads connected to the on-prem SAP landscape.

regions.name: UK South
regions.notes: Private only. Supports UK regional operations and on-prem connectivity.

regions.name: East US
regions.notes: Public/external subscriptions only. No corporate backbone connectivity is extended to US regions.

regions.name: East US 2
regions.notes: Paired region to East US for external disaster recovery.

regions.name: Central India
regions.notes: No private region. Public/external subscriptions only.

regions.name: Brazil South
regions.notes: Not enabled in the tenant. Region-locked pending data-sovereignty review; request via the Exception Catalog if required.

entries.name: Azure Virtual Machines
entries.description: IaaS virtual machines for general-purpose and specialized workloads.

vnet.notes: Standard building block for private workloads. Only approved VM SKUs per the size-governance policy may be provisioned.

external.notes: Approved for internet-facing workloads. Must sit behind an approved edge pattern (Application Gateway or Front Door) and hardened NSGs.

entries.name: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
entries.description: Managed Kubernetes container orchestration service.

vnet.notes: Allowed with mandatory Azure Policy add-on and private cluster configuration.

external.notes: Denied by default for external subscriptions due to the increased attack surface of an internet-facing control plane. Approvable via Deviation Request, mandating a private cluster behind the Front Door + WAF pattern.

entries.name: Azure App Service
entries.description: Fully managed platform for hosting web apps, REST APIs, and mobile back ends.

vnet.notes: Standard PaaS hosting option for private line-of-business applications.

external.notes: Standard PaaS hosting option for internet-facing applications; must be fronted by Front Door or Application Gateway per the edge pattern.

entries.name: Azure Functions
entries.description: Event-driven, serverless compute platform.

vnet.notes: Allowed on the Premium or App Service plan with VNet integration; Consumption plan requires the private-endpoint variant.

external.notes: Approved for lightweight internet-facing APIs and webhooks.

entries.name: Azure Front Door
entries.description: Global HTTP load balancer, CDN, and application-layer edge platform.

vnet.notes: Not permitted in private subscriptions under any deviation.

external.notes: Denied by default. Approvable via Deviation Request in the Exception Catalog for internet-facing apps only.

entries.name: Azure Application Gateway
entries.description: Regional layer-7 load balancer with an integrated web application firewall.

vnet.notes: Standard internal edge/ingress pattern. WAF_v2 SKU is mandatory.

external.notes: Standard external edge pattern for internet-facing apps not fronted by Front Door. WAF_v2 SKU is mandatory.

entries.name: Azure VPN Gateway
entries.description: Site-to-site and point-to-site VPN connectivity for a virtual network.

vnet.notes: Used for site-to-site connectivity to on-premises data centers alongside ExpressRoute.

external.notes: Not applicable. External subscriptions have no direct vNET/on-prem connectivity by design; use the Cloud Integration Platform for internal-external integration instead.

entries.name: Azure Firewall
entries.description: Managed, cloud-native network firewall and threat-protection service.

vnet.notes: Mandatory perimeter control for private subscriptions with internet egress; must be deployed per the central hub-spoke pattern.

external.notes: External subscriptions do not manage their own perimeter firewall. Edge protection is provided centrally via Front Door/WAF and the Cloud Integration Platform.

entries.name: Azure Content Delivery Network
entries.description: Global content-delivery network for caching static content close to users.

vnet.notes: Under evaluation by the network architecture board; not yet approved for general use in private subscriptions.

external.notes: Approved for static-content acceleration on public-facing sites.

entries.name: Azure Storage Account
entries.description: General-purpose object, blob, queue, table, and file storage.

vnet.notes: Standard storage service. Private endpoints required; public network access must be disabled.

external.notes: Standard storage service for internet-facing workloads. Public access restricted to explicit container/blob level with SAS or Front Door origin lock where applicable.

entries.name: Azure NetApp Files
entries.description: High-performance, low-latency managed file storage for enterprise workloads.

vnet.notes: Denied by default due to high fixed cost. Approvable via Deviation Request for workloads with a validated low-latency shared-file requirement (e.g. SAP, HPC).

external.notes: Not available to external subscriptions. No supported use case identified.

entries.name: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
entries.description: Hierarchical-namespace object storage optimized for big-data analytics.

vnet.notes: Allowed for team-scoped analytics datasets. For enterprise-wide analytics, prefer onboarding to the Enterprise Data Platform instead of standalone storage.

external.notes: Allowed for public dataset publishing scenarios with explicit access review.

entries.name: Azure SQL Database
entries.description: Fully managed PaaS relational database engine.

vnet.notes: Standard relational database option for private applications. Private endpoint required.

external.notes: Standard relational database option for internet-facing applications with public network access disabled outside of approved firewall rules.

entries.name: Azure Cosmos DB
entries.description: Globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database service.

vnet.notes: Approved for high-scale, low-latency NoSQL workloads. Private endpoint required.

external.notes: Approved for internet-facing workloads requiring global distribution.

entries.name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server
entries.description: Fully managed PostgreSQL database with flexible compute and storage scaling.

vnet.notes: Standard open-source relational database option for private workloads.

external.notes: Standard open-source relational database option for internet-facing workloads.

entries.name: Azure SQL Managed Instance
entries.description: Near-full SQL Server compatibility as a managed PaaS instance, deployed inside a subnet.

vnet.notes: Requires a dedicated delegated subnet; subject to a VM-equivalent patching SLA.

external.notes: Requires VNet injection, which is architecturally incompatible with external subscriptions.

entries.name: Azure AI Foundry
entries.description: Platform for building, evaluating, and deploying generative AI applications and agents.

vnet.notes: Denied by default; consume generative AI capabilities via the Enterprise AI Foundry Service instead.

external.notes: Denied by default; consume generative AI capabilities via the Enterprise AI Foundry Service instead.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Enterprise AI Foundry Service
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Centrally managed AI Foundry offering. Consume via the enterprise service instead of deploying your own.

entries.name: Azure OpenAI Service
entries.description: Managed access to OpenAI foundation models (GPT, embeddings, DALL-E) via Azure.

vnet.notes: Denied by default; consume via the Enterprise AI Foundry Service instead of deploying dedicated OpenAI resources.

external.notes: Denied by default; consume via the Enterprise AI Foundry Service instead of deploying dedicated OpenAI resources.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Enterprise AI Foundry Service
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Centrally managed AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI offering with a pre-approved model catalog and chargeback.

entries.name: Azure Machine Learning
entries.description: End-to-end platform for training, tuning, and operationalizing traditional ML models.

vnet.notes: Denied by default in favor of the Enterprise AI Foundry Service. Approvable via Deviation Request for specialized MLOps pipelines not yet supported centrally.

external.notes: Not available to external subscriptions.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Enterprise AI Foundry Service
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Centrally managed AI/ML platform covering both generative and traditional ML workloads.

entries.name: Azure AI Search
entries.description: Managed search-as-a-service with vector, keyword, and hybrid retrieval capabilities.

vnet.notes: Approved for private application search and retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) scenarios. Private endpoint required.

external.notes: Denied by default for external subscriptions pending a data-egress review requirement. Approvable case by case.

entries.name: Azure Service Bus
entries.description: Fully managed enterprise message broker with queues and publish/subscribe topics.

vnet.notes: Standard asynchronous messaging service within the private network boundary.

external.notes: External subscriptions cannot reach private Service Bus namespaces directly. Use the Cloud Integration Platform for internal-to-external messaging patterns.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Cloud Integration Platform
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Centrally managed integration layer for internal-external and cross-subscription communication patterns.

entries.name: Azure API Management
entries.description: Full lifecycle API gateway, developer portal, and policy-enforcement platform.

vnet.notes: Approved as the standard private API gateway pattern.

external.notes: Denied by default; the Cloud Integration Platform provides the standard external API gateway. Deviation approvable for specialized public API products.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Cloud Integration Platform
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Provides the standard managed API gateway for external-facing and cross-boundary APIs.

entries.name: Azure Logic Apps
entries.description: Low-code workflow orchestration and connector-based integration service.

vnet.notes: Approved for private workflow automation and system-to-system orchestration.

external.notes: Prefer the Cloud Integration Platform for external-facing orchestration. Deviation approvable for low-complexity, internal-only-triggered external workflows.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Cloud Integration Platform
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Standard orchestration layer for workflows that cross the internal-external boundary.

entries.name: Azure Key Vault
entries.description: Managed service for secrets, keys, and certificates.

vnet.notes: Mandatory for all applications storing secrets, keys, or certificates. Private endpoint required.

external.notes: Mandatory for all applications storing secrets, keys, or certificates.

entries.name: Azure Bastion
entries.description: Fully managed PaaS service providing secure RDP/SSH connectivity without public IPs on VMs.

vnet.notes: Standard secure-access pattern for jump access to private VMs.

external.notes: Not applicable; external subscriptions have no private network to jump into.

entries.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
entries.description: Cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) covering posture management and workload protection.

vnet.notes: Enabled centrally at the management-group level via Azure Policy. No subscription action required.

external.notes: Enabled centrally at the management-group level via Azure Policy. No subscription action required.

entries.name: Azure DevOps
entries.description: Suite of services for CI/CD pipelines, repos, boards, and test plans.

vnet.notes: Standard CI/CD platform. Microsoft-hosted or self-hosted agents both permitted subject to the runner policy.

external.notes: Standard CI/CD platform for teams owning external-subscription workloads.

entries.name: Self-hosted GitHub Actions Runners
entries.description: Self-managed VM or container-based runners for executing GitHub Actions workflows.

vnet.notes: Denied by default due to secrets-exposure risk on shared infrastructure. Approvable via Deviation Request with a mandatory runner-hardening baseline.

external.notes: Not permitted. Use GitHub-hosted runners, or the private-subscription pattern where separately approved.

entries.name: Azure Synapse Analytics
entries.description: Integrated analytics platform combining data warehousing, big-data processing, and pipelines.

vnet.notes: Superseded by the Enterprise Data Platform; use the central offering for enterprise analytics workloads.

external.notes: Not available to external subscriptions.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Enterprise Data Platform
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Central analytics and data-integration platform replacing individually deployed Synapse workspaces.

entries.name: Azure Data Factory
entries.description: Managed data-integration and ETL/ELT pipeline orchestration service.

vnet.notes: Denied by default in favor of the Enterprise Data Platform. Approvable via Deviation Request for isolated point-to-point integration needs not covered centrally.

external.notes: Not available to external subscriptions.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Enterprise Data Platform
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Central analytics and data-integration platform replacing individually deployed Data Factory instances.

entries.name: Azure DevTest Labs
entries.description: Self-service sandbox environments for development and testing with cost-control policies.

vnet.notes: Superseded by the Lab-as-a-Service enterprise offering.

external.notes: Superseded by the Lab-as-a-Service enterprise offering.

enterpriseServiceAlternative.name: Lab-as-a-Service
enterpriseServiceAlternative.description: Centrally managed sandbox and training-lab environments with automatic expiry and cost caps.
